title: Holistic pipeline failure detection: two-tier health check framework
summary: Architecture analysis for a unified health check framework in the orchestrator. The framework introduces a shared HealthCheck interface with two tiers: Tier 1 (programmatic checks for structural invariants — fast, deterministic, run on every lifecycle event) and Tier 2 (LLM-based agent inspector for semantic health — run at phase boundaries and on degraded signals). Existing mechanisms (startup reconciliation, container monitor) are migrated to the interface. New checks include phase output presence, state consistency, and repeated failure patterns. A HealthCheckRunner coordinates execution, applies results, and emits events for observability. The recommended approach is the unified HealthCheck interface with lazy context assembly, building bottom-up from types through runner to individual checks and lifecycle wiring.

problem_statement.description: Pipeline failure detection is a collection of ad-hoc mechanisms built reactively for specific failure modes. startup_reconciliation.py handles crash recovery at startup, container_monitor.py detects container exits at runtime, signals.py records agent self-reported errors, and multi_agent.py has a blunt max_waves=5 iteration cap. None share a common abstraction, none produce structured verdicts, and none can detect semantic failures — cases where infrastructure is healthy but agents failed to accomplish meaningful work.
problem_statement.motivating_incident: Issue-835: reviewer containers exited cleanly (exit code 0), all structural checks passed, but reviewers had nothing to review because coders' work never reached the remote. Current mechanisms cannot detect this class of failure.
goals: Define a shared HealthCheck interface with structured HealthResult verdicts (HEALTHY / DEGRADED / FAILED) and suggested actions (CONTINUE / FAIL_PIPELINE / ALERT / RETRY)
Migrate startup reconciliation (#839) and container monitor (#848) to the new interface without changing observable behavior
Add Tier 1 programmatic checks: phase output presence (commits on remote), state consistency (orchestrator vs Docker), repeated failure patterns
Add Tier 2 agent inspector: LLM-based semantic evaluation of agent work quality
Wire trigger points into lifecycle: STARTUP, RUNTIME_TICK, WAVE_COMPLETE, PHASE_COMPLETE, ON_DEMAND
Surface health check results via the existing EventBus/SSE system for observability
Persist health check results in pipeline state for debugging (capped rolling window)

startup_reconciliation.mechanism: reconcile_stale_containers(store, docker_client) runs once at startup from cli.py:cmd_serve(). Compares persisted RUNNING pipeline containers against live Docker set. Missing containers → agent marked FAILED → pipeline marked FAILED with error message 'Container not found at orchestrator startup'. No version check on save (startup-only, no concurrent writers). Returns int count of recovered pipelines.
startup_reconciliation.interface_gap: No structured verdict — returns int. No reason/action tuple. No event emission. Direct state mutation inline.

container_monitor.mechanism: ContainerMonitor class with background thread polling Docker every 10s (configurable check_interval). _check_container() detects state transitions via cached _container_states dict, emits ContainerEvent (STARTED/STOPPED/FAILED/REMOVED). create_pipeline_reconciliation_handler() subscribes to FAILED events and calls _reconcile_container_state() which scans all RUNNING pipelines for the failed container, marks containers/agents/pipelines FAILED with optimistic locking (expected_version).
container_monitor.interface_gap: Uses its own ContainerEvent type (not shared HealthResult). State mutation is inline in the handler via _reconcile_container_state(), not mediated through a runner. Periodic orphan cleanup every 60 iterations.

signal_handlers.mechanism: Agents self-report via POST /pipelines/{id}/signal. handle_error_signal records failure in contract via dispatcher. handle_complete_signal records success and checks wave/phase completion.
signal_handlers.interface_gap: Reactive (agent-initiated only). No proactive detection capability. Trusts agent self-reporting.

iteration_caps.mechanism: execute_all_waves(on_wave_complete, agent_prompts, max_waves=5). When max_waves exceeded, logs warning 'Max waves reached ({max_waves}), stopping execution' and breaks. No structured verdict, no pipeline status update.
iteration_caps.interface_gap: Silent stop. Pipeline not marked FAILED. No structured reason provided.

event_system.mechanism: EventBus with typed EventType StrEnum. Supports: PIPELINE_* (created/started/completed/failed/cancelled), PHASE_* (started/completed/failed), AGENT_* (started/completed/failed/timeout), CONTAINER_* (spawned/stopped/removed), DECISION_* (created/resolved), HEALTH_CHECK, ERROR. Pub/sub with wildcard subscriptions, async delivery via worker thread, event history (max 100). Singleton via get_event_bus(). Convenience emit_event() function.
event_system.readiness: EventType.HEALTH_CHECK already exists and is ready for health check result events. No new event types needed.

resilience_patterns.mechanism: agent_recovery.py: AgentRetryManager with RetryPolicy (IMMEDIATE/BACKOFF/ESCALATE/NO_RETRY), AgentRetryConfig (max_retries, retry_delay), RetryDecision. AgentCircuitBreaker with CircuitBreakerConfig (failure_threshold, reset_timeout). resilience.py: RetryConfig and RetryableError for general retry patterns.
resilience_patterns.relevance: HealthCheckRunner should consult AgentRetryManager/AgentCircuitBreaker before applying FAIL_PIPELINE action — if retries are available and the failure is retryable, trigger retry instead of termination.

state_persistence.mechanism: Git-backed pipeline state on orphan branch egg/pipeline-state. StateStore with per-pipeline locking via get_pipeline_state_lock() (threading.RLock + fcntl.flock). Optimistic versioning via save_pipeline(pipeline, expected_version=N) → VersionConflictError on mismatch. Pipeline.version incremented on each save.
state_persistence.relevance: Health check state mutations must use per-pipeline locking and optimistic versioning to avoid races with concurrent signal handlers and the container monitor thread.

existing_http_health.mechanism: Flask blueprint at /api/v1/health, /api/v1/ready, /api/v1/live. Basic service health — returns 200 with status='healthy'. No pipeline-level health checking.
existing_http_health.relevance: The on-demand pipeline health check endpoint should be added here, extending the existing health blueprint.

pipeline_models.key_models: Pipeline (id, status, current_phase, phases, config, version), PhaseExecution (phase, status, containers, agents, review_cycles, artifacts, error), AgentExecution (role, status, container_id, commit, outputs, error, retry_count), ContainerInfo (container_id, status, exit_code, agent_role), PipelineConfig (max_review_cycles, max_parallel_agents, etc.)
pipeline_models.relevance: HealthCheckResult model will be added here. PhaseExecution.health_checks field will store recent results.

key_files.role: Runtime container failure detection via Docker polling
key_files.changes_needed: Extract _reconcile_container_state() evaluation logic into a ContainerLivenessCheck implementing HealthCheck. Update create_pipeline_reconciliation_handler() to route through HealthCheckRunner. Monitor continues polling Docker and emitting ContainerEvents; the runner handles state mutation.
key_files.risk: Medium — concurrent thread with state access. Must preserve per-pipeline locking and optimistic versioning behavior.

key_files.role: Wave-based parallel agent execution with on_wave_complete callback
key_files.changes_needed: Wire on_wave_complete callback (line 545-546) to invoke HealthCheckRunner.run_checks(trigger=WAVE_COMPLETE). Pass wave results in PipelineHealthContext. Replace silent max_waves stop with structured health check result.
key_files.risk: Medium — on_wave_complete runs from execution thread; checks must not block indefinitely.

key_files.changes_needed: Invoke HealthCheckRunner.run_checks(trigger=PHASE_COMPLETE) after phase completion in _run_pipeline(). Act on HealthResult.action. Changes should be minimal — single function calls at well-defined lifecycle points.
key_files.risk: High — largest, most complex file. Changes must be surgical. No restructuring.

key_files.role: EventBus with pub/sub and EventType enum
key_files.changes_needed: None. EventType.HEALTH_CHECK already exists. Health check results emitted as events with structured data payload.
key_files.risk: None — no changes to EventBus itself.

key_files.risk: Low — additive endpoint on existing blueprint.

key_files.changes_needed: Initialize HealthCheckRunner with all checks registered. Replace direct reconcile_stale_containers() call with runner.run_checks(trigger=STARTUP).

key_files.role: Flask app creation and blueprint registration
key_files.changes_needed: Initialize HealthCheckRunner singleton at app creation. Make it accessible to routes (e.g., via app context or module-level getter).

approaches.name: Unified HealthCheck interface with HealthCheckRunner
approaches.description: Define HealthCheck ABC, HealthResult, PipelineHealthContext, and Tier/Trigger enums in a new orchestrator/health/ package. Implement HealthCheckRunner that manages a registry of checks, runs them at trigger points, and applies results (emit events, optionally fail pipeline). Migrate startup reconciliation and container monitor. Add new Tier 1 checks (phase output presence, state consistency, repeated failures) and Tier 2 agent inspector. Wire triggers into lifecycle.
pros: Clean, composable abstraction — new checks are just new HealthCheck implementations
Unified HealthResult model standardizes all failure detection output with structured verdicts and actions
HealthCheckRunner centralizes result handling (event emission, pipeline state mutation, retry consultation)
Trigger points declared on the check — easy to reason about which checks run when
Each check independently testable — inject mock PipelineHealthContext, assert HealthResult
EventType.HEALTH_CHECK already exists — observability via SSE for free
Lazy context assembly avoids expensive operations on fast triggers
Migration of existing mechanisms is mechanical — both follow gather→evaluate→mutate pattern
cons: New abstraction layer that all future failure detection must go through
Migration of existing mechanisms requires refactoring to separate evaluation from state mutation
PipelineHealthContext assembly adds complexity (lazy loading for git log, agent outputs)
Tier 2 agent inspector adds LLM API cost and latency at phase boundaries
New orchestrator/health/ package adds ~10 new files

approaches.name: Event-driven health evaluation (no new interface)
approaches.description: Extend the existing EventBus with new event types for health evaluation. Subscribe health evaluation functions as event handlers. Add new handlers for phase output presence and semantic checks alongside existing mechanisms. Keep startup reconciliation and container monitor as-is.
pros: No new abstraction — reuses existing EventBus pub/sub infrastructure
Minimal migration — existing mechanisms stay untouched
cons: No unified result model — each handler decides its own output format
Tier classification (programmatic vs agent) is implicit rather than explicit
Trigger management scattered across handler registrations instead of declared on checks
Harder to test individual checks in isolation (requires mocking EventBus)
Doesn't solve core problem — adds more ad-hoc handlers without shared structure
No centralized result application — each handler must implement its own state mutation

approaches.name: Tier 1 only (defer Tier 2 agent inspector to follow-up)
approaches.description: Implement approach A's HealthCheck interface and all Tier 1 programmatic checks. Defer Tier 2 (LLM-based agent inspector) to a follow-up issue. Establishes the interface cleanly for Tier 2 to slot into later.
pros: Reduced scope — delivers unified interface and highest-value checks without LLM complexity
Phase output presence check alone catches issue-835 scenario (no commits on remote → DEGRADED)
No API cost concerns for initial rollout
Establishes the interface cleanly; Tier 2 is purely additive later
cons: Defers semantic health evaluation that catches novel failure patterns
Some failures remain undetectable: reviewer reviewed nothing, coder changes don't address issue
Interface may need adjustment when Tier 2 is added if not designed with it in mind

recommended_approach.name: Unified HealthCheck interface with HealthCheckRunner
justification: The refine analysis recommended Option A and both refine reviewers (refine + agent-design) approved. The issue description provides a well-considered design for the full two-tier framework.

The interface pays for itself immediately. The HealthCheck/HealthResult/PipelineHealthContext trio provides a testable, composable abstraction that replaces ad-hoc state mutations with structured verdicts. Instead of scanning logs for reconciliation warnings, operators get typed results with reasons and suggested actions.

Migration is mechanical. Both startup_reconciliation.py and container_monitor.py already follow the 'gather context → evaluate condition → mutate state' pattern. Wrapping them in HealthCheck.check() with HealthResult return is straightforward. State mutation moves to HealthCheckRunner._apply_result().

Tier 2 should ship in the same change to establish the full framework. This validates the interface handles both tiers cleanly and avoids the risk of designing for Tier 1 only and needing to adjust when Tier 2 arrives. The Tier 2 inspector is scoped (Haiku model, structured evaluation, 30s timeout) and the LLM call pattern is well-understood.

The codebase has the infrastructure: EventType.HEALTH_CHECK exists, per-pipeline locking is battle-tested, resilience patterns (AgentRetryManager, AgentCircuitBreaker) are available for retry consultation.

stages.name: Foundation: types, interface, and runner
stages.description: Define core abstractions in new orchestrator/health/ package. This is the foundation everything else builds on.

phases.name: Health check types and interface
phases.description: Create the core type definitions and abstract base class for the health check framework.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/__init__.py — package init with public API exports

New orchestrator/health/types.py — HealthStatus enum (HEALTHY/DEGRADED/FAILED), Action enum (CONTINUE/FAIL_PIPELINE/ALERT/RETRY), Tier enum (PROGRAMMATIC/AGENT), Trigger enum (STARTUP/RUNTIME_TICK/WAVE_COMPLETE/PHASE_COMPLETE/ON_DEMAND), HealthResult dataclass (status, reason, action, check_name, tier, timestamp, metadata dict)

New orchestrator/health/context.py — PipelineHealthContext with lazy-loaded properties: pipeline (eager), phase_execution (eager), containers (eager), agents (eager), git_log (lazy — subprocess git log on worktree), git_diff (lazy — subprocess git diff), agent_output_files (lazy — filesystem glob), wave_results (optional, passed for WAVE_COMPLETE triggers). Lazy fields use @cached_property or explicit _loaded flags.

New orchestrator/health/base.py — abstract HealthCheck class with abstract properties tier -> Tier, triggers -> list[Trigger], name -> str, and abstract method check(context: PipelineHealthContext) -> HealthResult

phases.name: HealthCheckRunner
phases.description: Implement the central runner that manages check registration, trigger filtering, execution, and result application.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/runner.py — HealthCheckRunner class with: register(check: HealthCheck) adds to registry, run_checks(trigger: Trigger, context: PipelineHealthContext) -> list[HealthResult] filters checks by trigger, runs Tier 1 first, escalates to Tier 2 if Tier 1 returns DEGRADED or trigger is PHASE_COMPLETE/ON_DEMAND. _apply_result(result, pipeline_id) emits HEALTH_CHECK event via emit_event(), persists result to PhaseExecution.health_checks (capped at 10), and for FAIL_PIPELINE action: consults AgentRetryManager — if retries available trigger retry, else mark pipeline FAILED. Uses per-pipeline locking for state mutations. Configurable per-check timeout (default 5s for Tier 1, 30s for Tier 2).

stages.name: Migrate existing mechanisms
stages.description: Wrap startup reconciliation and container monitor detection logic in HealthCheck implementations. Preserve exact existing behavior.

phases.name: Migrate startup reconciliation
phases.description: Extract startup reconciliation logic into a HealthCheck implementation.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/__init__.py — package init

New orchestrator/health/checks/startup.py — StartupReconciliationCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=PROGRAMMATIC, triggers=[STARTUP], name='startup_reconciliation'. check(context) compares persisted RUNNING containers against live Docker set (via docker_client in context). Returns FAILED if stale containers found (with list of affected pipeline/container IDs in reason), HEALTHY otherwise. Does NOT mutate state — runner handles that.

Modify orchestrator/cli.py — replace direct reconcile_stale_containers() call with runner.run_checks(trigger=STARTUP). The runner's _apply_result() handles marking pipelines FAILED, preserving the same error messages.
Keep orchestrator/startup_reconciliation.py — deprecate reconcile_stale_containers() but keep as thin wrapper calling StartupReconciliationCheck for backward compat if anything imports it directly

phases.name: Migrate container monitor detection
phases.description: Extract container failure reconciliation logic into a HealthCheck implementation.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/container_liveness.py — ContainerLivenessCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=PROGRAMMATIC, triggers=[RUNTIME_TICK], name='container_liveness'. check(context) takes failed container info from context, scans RUNNING pipelines for the container, returns FAILED if pipeline has stale container(s), HEALTHY otherwise. Does NOT mutate state.

Modify orchestrator/container_monitor.py — update create_pipeline_reconciliation_handler() to create handler that invokes HealthCheckRunner.run_checks(trigger=RUNTIME_TICK) with context containing the failed container info, instead of calling _reconcile_container_state() directly. Keep _reconcile_container_state() as deprecated backward-compat wrapper.

stages.name: New Tier 1 programmatic checks
stages.description: Add programmatic checks that detect failure modes not currently covered.

phases.name: Phase output presence check
phases.description: Check that phases produced expected artifacts. This is the check that would have caught issue-835.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/phase_output.py — PhaseOutputPresenceCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=PROGRAMMATIC, triggers=[PHASE_COMPLETE, WAVE_COMPLETE], name='phase_output_presence'. check(context) evaluates based on current phase: implement → checks git log for new commits on remote worktree branch since phase.work_started_at (uses context.git_log lazy property), plan → checks .egg-state/agent-outputs/ for architect/task_planner output files, refine → checks .egg-state/drafts/ for analysis document. Returns DEGRADED if expected outputs missing (not FAILED — gives Tier 2 a chance to evaluate), HEALTHY if present.

phases.name: State consistency check
phases.description: Verify orchestrator state matches Docker reality during runtime.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/state_consistency.py — StateConsistencyCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=PROGRAMMATIC, triggers=[WAVE_COMPLETE, PHASE_COMPLETE], name='state_consistency'. check(context) verifies: containers marked RUNNING in pipeline state actually exist and are running in Docker (via docker_client), agents marked RUNNING have corresponding running containers, pipeline marked RUNNING has at least one active phase with active containers. Returns DEGRADED on drift (some containers gone), FAILED on critical inconsistency (all containers gone but pipeline RUNNING).

phases.name: Repeated failure pattern check
phases.description: Detect agents failing repeatedly with the same error, replacing the blunt max_waves cap.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/failure_patterns.py — RepeatedFailureCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=PROGRAMMATIC, triggers=[WAVE_COMPLETE], name='repeated_failure_pattern'. check(context) examines agent execution history in current phase: if same role failed N times (configurable, default 3) with same/similar error, returns FAILED with action FAIL_PIPELINE and reason containing error pattern. Optionally consults AgentCircuitBreaker state if available. Replaces the blunt max_waves silent stop with a smarter detection that explains why it's failing.

stages.name: Tier 2 agent inspector
stages.description: Implement LLM-based semantic health evaluation for detecting novel failure patterns.

phases.name: LLM client for orchestrator
phases.description: Thin wrapper for Anthropic API calls from the orchestrator context.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/llm_client.py — HealthInspectorClient class wrapping Anthropic API. Uses Haiku model for cost efficiency. Configurable model (default: claude-haiku). Structured output via JSON mode. Timeout: 30 seconds. Handles API errors gracefully (returns None on failure — inspector treats this as CONTINUE). Uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from environment (available via gateway proxy in both network modes).

phases.name: Agent inspector implementation
phases.description: LLM-based check that evaluates whether agents produced meaningful work matching the phase goal.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/agent_inspector.py — AgentInspectorCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=AGENT, triggers=[PHASE_COMPLETE, ON_DEMAND], name='agent_inspector'. check(context) assembles structured prompt with: (1) phase goal from contract, (2) agent output files content (context.agent_output_files), (3) git log/diff on worktree branch (context.git_log, context.git_diff), (4) agent execution results (success/fail/error messages). Prompt asks LLM to evaluate: did agents produce work matching the phase goal? Is the work substantive or empty? Are there signs of stuck/looping behavior? Did reviewers actually review? LLM returns structured JSON verdict: {status: 'HEALTHY'|'DEGRADED'|'FAILED', reasoning: str, suggested_action: str}. Parses response into HealthResult. On LLM failure (timeout, API error, malformed response): returns DEGRADED with action CONTINUE and reason explaining inspector failure.

stages.name: Lifecycle wiring and observability
stages.description: Wire health check trigger points into the orchestrator lifecycle and persist results.

phases.name: Pipeline state model extension
phases.description: Add health check result persistence to the pipeline state model.
key_changes: Modify orchestrator/models.py — add HealthCheckResult model (Pydantic BaseModel with: check_name: str, tier: str, status: str, reason: str, action: str, timestamp: datetime, metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}). Add health_checks: list[HealthCheckResult] = Field(default_factory=list) to PhaseExecution. Backward compatible — defaults to empty list.

phases.name: Wire trigger points into lifecycle
phases.description: Integrate HealthCheckRunner into the orchestrator's main execution paths.
key_changes: Modify orchestrator/api.py — create HealthCheckRunner singleton at app creation, register all checks (StartupReconciliation, ContainerLiveness, PhaseOutputPresence, StateConsistency, RepeatedFailure, AgentInspector). Expose via module-level getter.
Modify orchestrator/cli.py — replace reconcile_stale_containers() with runner.run_checks(trigger=STARTUP)
Modify orchestrator/container_monitor.py — update create_pipeline_reconciliation_handler() to use runner
Modify orchestrator/multi_agent.py — ensure on_wave_complete callback invokes runner.run_checks(trigger=WAVE_COMPLETE)

Modify orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py — invoke runner.run_checks(trigger=PHASE_COMPLETE) after phase completion in _run_pipeline(). Act on results: FAIL_PIPELINE → mark pipeline failed, RETRY → trigger agent retry, ALERT → emit event only, CONTINUE → proceed.
Modify orchestrator/routes/health.py — add POST /api/v1/pipelines/<pipeline_id>/health-check endpoint for on-demand evaluation. Returns aggregated health results.

stages.name: Testing
stages.description: Comprehensive test coverage for the health check framework.

phases.name: Unit tests for types, context, and individual checks
phases.description: Test each component independently with mock dependencies.
key_changes: New orchestrator/tests/test_health_types.py — test HealthResult creation, HealthStatus/Action/Tier/Trigger enums
New orchestrator/tests/test_health_context.py — test PipelineHealthContext lazy loading, test that expensive fields aren't computed until accessed

New orchestrator/tests/test_health_checks.py — test each HealthCheck implementation: StartupReconciliation (mock Docker, verify HEALTHY/FAILED), ContainerLiveness (mock pipeline state, verify detection), PhaseOutputPresence (mock git/filesystem, verify DEGRADED on missing outputs), StateConsistency (mock Docker vs state, verify drift detection), RepeatedFailure (mock execution history, verify pattern detection), AgentInspector (mock LLM client, verify structured verdict parsing and graceful failure handling)

phases.name: Unit tests for runner and integration tests for lifecycle
phases.description: Test the runner and end-to-end lifecycle wiring.
key_changes: New orchestrator/tests/test_health_runner.py — test HealthCheckRunner: trigger filtering (only matching checks run), Tier 1→Tier 2 escalation (DEGRADED triggers Tier 2), result application (FAIL_PIPELINE with retry consultation, event emission, result persistence, cap at 10 results), concurrent execution safety (per-pipeline locking)

New orchestrator/tests/test_health_integration.py — test lifecycle wiring: startup trigger runs startup check, container failure triggers runtime check, wave complete triggers wave checks, phase complete triggers all checks including Tier 2, on-demand REST endpoint returns results. Mock Docker and LLM API throughout.
Verify backward compatibility: migrated startup reconciliation produces same state changes as original. Migrated container monitor produces same state changes as original.

technical_decisions.decision: New orchestrator/health/ package rather than extending existing files
technical_decisions.rationale: The health check framework is a cohesive concern with its own types, interface, runner, and check implementations. orchestrator/health/ follows the same sub-package pattern as orchestrator/routes/. Avoids bloating existing files (especially the 5500-line routes/pipelines.py). Keeps checks independently testable and discoverable.
alternatives_considered: Add to container_monitor.py — rejected: mixes runtime monitoring with broader health check concern
Add to routes/pipelines.py — rejected: already 5500 lines, health checks aren't HTTP route logic
Flat files in orchestrator/ — rejected: 8+ new files would clutter the top-level directory

technical_decisions.rationale: Some fields are expensive: git log/diff requires subprocess calls to git, agent output files require filesystem reads. Runtime tick triggers happen every 10 seconds — eagerly computing all fields would add unnecessary overhead. Lazy properties (@cached_property or explicit flags) ensure a check that only needs container state never triggers git operations. Context objects are short-lived (per trigger invocation), so caching doesn't cause staleness.
alternatives_considered: Eager assembly with caching — rejected: cache invalidation is complex and most checks only need a subset
Pass raw pipeline object, let checks gather their own context — rejected: couples checks to orchestrator internals, prevents testing with mock context
Pre-filter context based on check requirements — rejected: over-engineering, lazy loading achieves same result naturally

technical_decisions.decision: Tier 2 agent inspector uses Haiku model
technical_decisions.rationale: The inspector's task is structured evaluation against a checklist: did agents produce work, is it substantive, any signs of looping. The input is well-defined (agent outputs, git diff, execution results) and output is a structured JSON verdict. Haiku handles this well, is fast (~1-2s), and cheap. If Haiku proves insufficient for nuanced semantic evaluation, the model can be upgraded per-check without interface changes.
alternatives_considered: Use Sonnet/Opus (same as agent sandboxes) — rejected: expensive and slow for a supervisory check at every phase boundary
No LLM (pattern matching only) — rejected: cannot detect novel failure modes, which is the core value of Tier 2
Configurable model per pipeline — considered but deferred: start with Haiku default, add config if needed

technical_decisions.decision: HealthCheckRunner applies results centrally — checks are pure evaluation functions
technical_decisions.rationale: Checks should be pure: context in, result out. The runner handles side effects (event emission, pipeline state mutation, retry consultation, result persistence). This makes checks independently testable without requiring a real state store, prevents duplicate state mutations from concurrent checks, and centralizes the decision logic for what to do with a FAIL_PIPELINE result (e.g., consult AgentRetryManager first).
alternatives_considered: Checks mutate state directly (current container_monitor pattern) — rejected: scatters mutation logic, requires real state store for testing
Checks return results, caller applies at each trigger point — rejected: duplicates application logic across 5 trigger points

technical_decisions.decision: Health check results persisted in PhaseExecution.health_checks, capped at 10
technical_decisions.rationale: Results need persistence for debugging and observability but must not bloat pipeline state JSON. PhaseExecution is the natural home — health checks evaluate phase-level health. A rolling window of 10 results per phase provides enough history for recent failure diagnosis without unbounded growth. At ~200 bytes per result, 10 results adds ~2KB per phase — negligible relative to the typical pipeline state.
alternatives_considered: Separate .egg-state/health/{pipeline-id}.json — rejected: adds another artifact with separate lifecycle management
Only emit events, don't persist — rejected: events are ephemeral (100 max in EventBus history), debugging needs historical results
Store in Pipeline.health_checks (top-level) — rejected: loses phase-level granularity, less natural for phase-scoped checks

technical_decisions.decision: Tier 2 triggers: always at PHASE_COMPLETE, at WAVE_COMPLETE only on DEGRADED from Tier 1
technical_decisions.rationale: PHASE_COMPLETE is the natural checkpoint for semantic evaluation — the phase is done and we need to assess work quality before advancing. Running Tier 2 at every WAVE_COMPLETE would be expensive (LLM calls per wave). The DEGRADED trigger provides escalation: if Tier 1 detects structural anomalies (missing outputs, state drift), Tier 2 evaluates whether the anomaly is a real failure or benign edge case. ON_DEMAND via REST endpoint covers ad-hoc investigation.
alternatives_considered: Tier 2 at every trigger — rejected: prohibitive LLM cost
Tier 2 only on-demand — rejected: defeats automatic detection purpose
Tier 2 on a timer — rejected: not correlated with meaningful lifecycle events
Tier 2 only at PHASE_COMPLETE, never at WAVE_COMPLETE — considered but escalation from DEGRADED is valuable for catching issues mid-phase before all waves complete

technical_decisions.decision: FAIL_PIPELINE action is automatic but consulted against retry logic
technical_decisions.rationale: Advisory-only FAIL_PIPELINE risks being ignored (no handler watching → silent failure). Automatic enforcement ensures health check results have teeth. However, the runner consults AgentRetryManager before failing: if the failure is retryable and retries remain, trigger retry instead of terminating the pipeline. This bridges health checks and the recovery system. If retries are exhausted or the circuit breaker is open, proceed with FAIL_PIPELINE.
alternatives_considered: Advisory only (emit event, let caller decide) — rejected: existing code doesn't watch for health events, failure would be silently ignored
Always fail immediately (no retry) — rejected: some failures are transient, retrying is cheaper than failing the whole pipeline
Separate RETRY action — implemented: checks can return Action.RETRY explicitly to request retry without FAIL

technical_decisions.decision: Inspector failures treated as DEGRADED/CONTINUE, not blocking
technical_decisions.rationale: The agent inspector is a safety net, not a gate. If the LLM API is down, returns malformed output, or times out, the pipeline should not be blocked. Returning DEGRADED with CONTINUE means the failure is logged and visible in health check results but doesn't prevent phase advancement. This avoids a scenario where Anthropic API outage blocks all pipelines.
alternatives_considered: Block on inspector failure — rejected: makes pipeline availability dependent on LLM API availability
Skip silently — rejected: losing visibility into inspector failures hinders debugging

risks.description: routes/pipelines.py is 5543 lines and the central orchestration point. Wiring health check triggers into _run_pipeline() requires surgical changes to a complex control flow with review cycles, phase transitions, and error handling.
risks.mitigation: Keep integration points minimal — single runner.run_checks() calls at well-defined lifecycle events. The runner encapsulates all complexity. Integration sites pass trigger and context only. No structural changes to _run_pipeline().

risks.description: Health checks run on lifecycle events from concurrent threads: RUNTIME_TICK from monitor thread, WAVE_COMPLETE from execution thread, ON_DEMAND from HTTP thread. Multiple checks trying to fail the same pipeline simultaneously could cause optimistic locking conflicts.
risks.mitigation: HealthCheckRunner uses per-pipeline locking (get_pipeline_state_lock) and optimistic versioning (expected_version) — same patterns as _reconcile_container_state() today. On VersionConflictError, reload pipeline and re-evaluate rather than retrying the state mutation blindly. Short-circuit if pipeline is already FAILED.

risks.description: Tier 1 checks run on every lifecycle event including 10-second runtime ticks. Slow checks (git operations on large repos) could delay the monitor loop and miss container failures.
risks.mitigation: Lazy context assembly ensures expensive operations (git log, file reads) only run when accessed. Runtime tick checks (container liveness) only need in-memory state and Docker API — no git operations. Per-check timeout: 5s default for Tier 1. Phase output check (which needs git) only runs on PHASE_COMPLETE/WAVE_COMPLETE, not RUNTIME_TICK.

risks.description: Tier 2 agent inspector depends on LLM API availability and response quality. API outage, malformed output, or incorrect verdict could impact pipeline operations.
risks.mitigation: Inspector failures → DEGRADED/CONTINUE (not blocking). 30-second timeout. JSON mode for structured output. Structured prompt with explicit verdict format reduces parsing failures. False positive rate managed by requiring high confidence for FAILED verdict.

risks.description: Migrating startup reconciliation and container monitor to the new interface could change observable behavior (error messages, state mutation timing, event emission).
risks.mitigation: Preserve exact error messages. Add comparison tests: run original function and migrated check on same input, verify same pipeline state mutations. Keep original functions as deprecated wrappers during transition.

risks.description: Tier 2 agent inspector makes LLM API calls at phase boundaries. In a multi-phase pipeline with review cycles, this could accumulate non-trivial costs.
risks.mitigation: Use Haiku (cheapest model). Typical pipeline: 3-4 phases × 1 PHASE_COMPLETE each = 3-4 Haiku calls. At ~$0.001/call, total cost per pipeline is under $0.01. DEGRADED escalation at WAVE_COMPLETE adds occasional extra calls. Configurable model and can disable Tier 2 per pipeline if needed.

constraints: Tier 1 checks must be sub-second — no LLM calls, minimal git operations (use lazy context)
Tier 2 checks must not block phase transitions — 30-second timeout, treat failures as CONTINUE
Per-pipeline locking (get_pipeline_state_lock) and optimistic versioning (expected_version) required for all state mutations
Health check results capped at 10 per PhaseExecution to prevent state bloat
Backward compatibility: migrated startup reconciliation and container monitor must preserve existing error messages and state mutations
Network mode awareness: Tier 2 inspector works in both public and private modes (Anthropic API available in both via gateway proxy)
Each HealthCheck must be independently testable with mock PipelineHealthContext — no singleton access to Docker or state store inside check logic
HealthCheckRunner must be thread-safe — concurrent triggers from monitor, execution, and HTTP threads
No new EventType needed — use existing EventType.HEALTH_CHECK with structured data payload

open_questions_resolved.question: Should Tier 2 use the same model as agent sandboxes or a smaller model?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Use Haiku (TD-3). Structured evaluation task, not open-ended reasoning. Fast and cheap. Upgradeable per-check.

open_questions_resolved.question: Should FAIL_PIPELINE action be automatic or advisory?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Automatic but consulted against retry logic (TD-7). Runner checks AgentRetryManager before failing — retries first if available.

open_questions_resolved.question: Where should health check results be persisted?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: PhaseExecution.health_checks, capped at 10 (TD-5). Keeps phase state in one place, avoids separate artifact lifecycle.

open_questions_resolved.question: What triggers Tier 2?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Always at PHASE_COMPLETE. At WAVE_COMPLETE only if Tier 1 returned DEGRADED. On-demand via REST endpoint (TD-6).

open_questions_resolved.question: Should health checks interact with AgentRetryManager?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Yes (TD-7). Runner consults retry/circuit-breaker logic before applying FAIL_PIPELINE. Bridges health check and recovery systems.
